clue.text: Won't give crushed ice in salt.

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining an adjective: something that won't give or stretch

indicators.note: crushed ice is broken up, so the letters of these words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ice packed in salt is crushed but refuses to yield.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelastic has no stretch, so it does not yield under pressure.

clue.text: It should bring good luck to a on the race-course.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'It should bring good luck to a on the race-course.': a word after 'a' is missing (the piece that goes round ASCOT), no scan to restore it
annotationWithheld.clue: It should bring good luck to a on the race-course.

clue.text: Uninterested in the implication boat's not sinking?

definitions.meaning: a boat that leans over less is listing less, read as the phrase 'lists less'

explanation.surface: A bored sailor is unmoved by news that the vessel is staying afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless describes someone apathetic, without energy or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Positively the final demonstration cobbler?

definitions.meaning: a show that is definitely the end of the run
a shoemaker's foot-shaped form is called a last, so his show is punningly his last one

explanation.definitionFit: A positively final show is the closing one of a run.

clue.text: Anyone offering praise to a beauty or a nice car?

definitions.meaning: any person at all, an unnamed individual

definitions.text: offering praise to a beauty or a nice car?
definitions.meaning: admiring an attractive figure or a car's fine bodywork you might say 'that's ...'

explanation.surface: Who would compliment both a pretty woman and a smart motor?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an unspecified person, much like anyone.

clue.text: Measured and padded.

definitions.meaning: marked out with ruled lines, as on paper
given a lining or inner layer, as a coat

explanation.definitionFit: Ruled paper has lines marked on it, and a padded jacket has a lining sewn in.

clue.text: Keep on rushing up, doctor!

parts.note: to surge is to rush or rise up suddenly

explanation.surface: An urgent cry to keep pressing on in a hurry, Doc!
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner who operates, a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Not exactly all my eye!

parts.note: 'all my eye' is slang for nonsense, but read literally it names only one transparent part of the eyeball, not the whole thing

explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the clear front layer of the eye, only part of it.

clue.text: Half-tangled yarn about a school.

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half

indicators.note: tangled thread is jumbled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A partly knotted ball of wool is somehow connected with a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college, especially one training priests.

clue.text: It's quite plain that there's a in the doorway.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'It's quite plain that there's a in the doorway.': a word after 'a' is missing (the piece that goes inside EXIT), no scan to restore it
annotationWithheld.clue: It's quite plain that there's a in the doorway.

clue.text: He may expect a lot, though lifting a finger.

definitions.text: He may expect a lot, though lifting a finger.

parts.words: He may expect a lot, though lifting a finger.
parts.note: at an auction a buyer raises a finger to signal an offer for a lot, though he barely lifts a finger

explanation.definitionFit: At a sale-room, someone making offers hopes to win the lot.

clue.text: I sent tea out to appear cordial.

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Sending out tea makes me seem friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is an aniseed liqueur, and a cordial is an old word for such a sweet liqueur.

clue.text: Revolutionary bit of machinery helps to provide a bird with colourful legs!

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
a shank is the shaft of a tool or machine part

explanation.surface: A rebel and a machine part combine to give a brightly legged bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redshank is a wading bird named for its red legs.

clue.text: Transmits in succession, with complete ease.

definitions.meaning: passes on from one generation to the next

explanation.definitionFit: Heirlooms are passed on through families, and an easy victory is won effortlessly.

clue.text: Did he ride for Cromwell or turn up inside out?

indicators.note: to turn something up is to churn it over, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether a Roundhead trooper rode, or tumbled with his coat inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War were nicknamed Ironsides.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironside was the nickname of Cromwell and his troopers, the Puritan cavalry.

clue.text: Nothing is added to public by this composition.

indicators.note: the zero is attached at the end of the other piece

parts.note: a concert is a public performance of music
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is contributed to the public good by this piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a piece of music for soloist and orchestra.

clue.text: A tour we reorganised to last longer.

indicators.note: reorganised means arranged differently, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A rearranged holiday itinerary might stretch on further.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear is to remain in use for longer than something else.

clue.text: Run into a bullet by the sound of it when getting rid of the waste!

indicators.note: into says the first word goes inside the second piece

parts.words: a bullet by the sound of it
parts.note: a ping is the noise a bullet makes in flight or ricochet

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles into a whizzing bullet while clearing rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' is no homophone here: it describes the noise PING.
explanation.definitionFit: Pruning means cutting away dead or surplus growth.

clue.text: Those who go in for cycles as petitive sport?

definitions.text: Those who go in for cycles
definitions.meaning: people who make circuits or laps
a British bat-and-ball game like baseball

explanation.surface: Cyclists take up racing as a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUNDERS is a bat-and-ball game played in British schools, close to baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: The game is named for running round bases, and the word also means people going round.

clue.text: Not accustomed to mint?

explanation.definitionFit: A new arrival is not used to things, and a stamp in mint condition has never been used.

clue.text: Natural tendency in one's song.

definitions.meaning: a tune or passage of melody in music

explanation.surface: An inborn trait shows in how one sings.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is an inherited streak of character, and also a tune or musical passage.

clue.text: Accumulate by giving service.

definitions.meaning: a Mass is a church service, so this reads as 'a Mass'

explanation.definitionFit: To pile up is to gather, and a church Mass is a religious service.

clue.text: Aunt gets mixed up with the band, that more than enough for you?

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled together, so the two words' letters are combined and reordered

explanation.surface: An aunt joins the band; is that too much for you?
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, existing in great supply.

clue.text: A mere nothing for instance in set of people.

indicators.note: in places the example abbreviation within the people

parts.note: a nation is a body of people
EG, from Latin exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: A tiny nothing found, for example, in a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A negation is a denial or nullity, a mere nothing.

clue.text: Girl in need of new aid.

indicators.note: these letters need sorting out, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman wants fresh help.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwina is a female first name.

clue.text: Greenery cut short sheer by the lake.

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is removed

parts.note: mere means sheer, utter, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: Lawn trimmed sheer down by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASMERE is a lake and village in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasmere is one of the lakes of Cumbria's Lake District.
